$description: ViaVitae spacing tokens, on a 4pt base scale. Every margin, padding, gap and inset in the system is one of these values. An off-scale value is a defect that shows up as a page that looks almost right and cannot be fixed by anyone who did not build it, because the difference between 18px and 16px is invisible in isolation and obvious across a screen. The only permitted exception is a hairline border width, which lives in its own group below at 1px and is not part of the scale.

meta.$description: Non-DTCG bookkeeping, ignored by DTCG-conformant tooling.
meta.name: spacing

spacing.$description: The scale. Steps are named by their multiple of the 4pt base, not by their pixel value, so the scale can be re-based without renaming every consumer: spacing.4 means four base units and is 16px at the current base. Values below 16px are dense and used inside components; values from 16px up are layout and used between them. The jump from 3 to 4 to 6 skips 5 deliberately — a 20px gap is almost always a mistake for 16px or 24px, and removing it removes the mistake.

0.$description: Zero. Used for reset and for adjacent-sibling margin collapsing.

px.$description: Half-step, off-scale by design. Optical alignment only — nudging an icon one pixel onto a text baseline. Not a layout value.

0-5.$description: Half a base unit. The gap between a checkbox and its label.

1.$description: One base unit. Icon-to-label gap, badge padding, inline chip spacing.

2.$description: Two base units. Tight component padding, gap between related form fields, list item spacing.

3.$description: Three base units. Standard button padding-y, input padding, gap inside a card header.

4.$description: Four base units. THE default. Card padding, gap between stacked sections inside a component, page gutter on mobile.

6.$description: Six base units. Gap between cards in a grid, section padding on tablet, paragraph spacing in long-form prose.

8.$description: Eight base units. Space above an h2, page gutter on desktop.

10.$description: Ten base units. Gap between a hero and the first content section.

12.$description: Twelve base units. Section separation on mobile and tablet.

16.$description: Sixteen base units. Section separation on desktop.

20.$description: Twenty base units. Major page division — between the hero and the body, or between two distinct scroll-story chapters.

24.$description: Twenty-four base units. Largest standard section gap. Above this, a section break reads as two pages rather than one.

32.$description: Thirty-two base units. Reserved for the top and bottom of a marketing page, where the extra air is the design.

40.$description: Forty base units. Reserved for full-bleed scroll-story transitions on a product page.

48.$description: Forty-eight base units. The ceiling. Nothing in the system needs more; if a layout does, the layout is wrong.

component.$description: Composite spacing: named component paddings built from the scale above. Declared as aliases so a change to spacing.4 propagates. These exist because 'the padding inside a button' is a design decision that should be made once, not re-derived in every component file.

button-padding-x-lg.$description: 24px horizontal padding on a large button.

button-padding-y-lg.$description: 12px vertical padding on a large button. With the button-lg label at 17px and 1.2 line-height that is a 20.4px line box plus 24px of padding, giving a 44.4px control — clear of the 44px touch-target guidance and well clear of the 24px floor in WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8.

button-padding-y-md.$description: 8px vertical on the 15px button-md label gives an 18px line box plus 16px of padding, a 34px control. That is above the 24px AA floor but below the 44px guidance, so reset.css grows an md button to lg padding under (pointer: coarse) where a finger rather than a cursor is doing the aiming.

input-padding-y.$description: 12px vertical on the 16px body-md label at 1.6 line-height gives a 25.6px line box plus 24px of padding, a 49.6px field. A form control is a primary target and is sized accordingly.

card-padding.$description: 24px on all sides. Grows to spacing.8 above the lg breakpoint.

icon-label-gap.$description: 8px between an icon and its label. Tighter than the general scale because the two form a single perceptual unit.

focus-ring-offset.$description: 2px gap between a control's edge and its focus ring. Without the offset the ring merges with the control's own border and the focus state becomes ambiguous, particularly on a dark surface where a navy control meets a navy background.

focus-ring-width.$description: 2px ring. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 requires the focus indicator to enclose an area at least equal to a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter of the unfocused component, so 1px fails regardless of contrast. With the 2px offset the indicator reads as a distinct band of colour rather than as a border, which is the point of the offset.

layout.$description: Page-level spacing: gutters, container widths and the vertical rhythm between sections. Gutters are responsive and step at the breakpoints in breakpoints.json.

gutter.$description: 16px page gutter below the md breakpoint.

gutter-xl.$description: 48px from 1280px. The gutter stops growing here: beyond 48px a wide monitor wastes the space the content should use.

container-max.$description: Maximum content width. Matches the xl breakpoint so a container never exceeds the viewport it was designed at.

container-prose.$description: Maximum width for a long-form reading column, chosen so body-lg at 18px lands near the 66ch optimal measure in typography.json.

container-wide.$description: Maximum width for a full-bleed data table or a gallery grid. Matches the 2xl breakpoint.

section-gap.$description: 64px between sections on desktop; steps down to spacing.12 at md and spacing.8 at sm.

grid-gap.$description: 24px between cards in a marketing grid. Tighter than section-gap on purpose: items in a grid must read as one group.

stack-gap.$description: 16px between stacked elements inside a section.

border.$description: Border widths, kept out of the spacing scale because they are not spacing. Declared here so a component never invents a border weight.

hairline.$description: Default border, divider, input outline, table rule.

medium.$description: Emphasis border, selected card, the focus ring itself.

heavy.$description: Accent bar at the top of a featured card, the left rule on a pull quote. The heaviest border in the system.

com.viavitae.rationale.$description: Why 4pt and not 8pt. An 8pt grid is the common choice and is fine for a product UI, but it cannot express the 4px and 12px gaps that icon-and-label and input-padding actually need, so a team on an 8pt grid ends up with off-scale values everywhere and no grid at all. 4pt is the smallest base that still forces alignment: it permits 4, 8, 12, 16 and every multiple, so nothing needs to go off-scale. The cost is that a 4pt grid permits more values than an 8pt grid and therefore more choices — which is what the component and layout groups above exist to remove.
com.viavitae.rationale.rejected: 8pt grid — cannot express 4px icon gaps or 12px input padding without breaking itself.
com.viavitae.rationale.touchTargetFloor: 44px, per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), which specifies 24 CSS pixels as the AA minimum and 44 as the established platform guidance for a primary control. This system targets 44 for anything primary and 24 as the absolute floor, with the 24 floor reached only by an inline icon inside a link whose whole line box is the target.
